sanskrit: prītipravṛttau vinivartane tathā; suhṛtsu vijñāya nivṛtya cobhayoḥ yad eva mitraṃ gurubhāram āvahet; tad eva susnigdham udāhared budhaḥ
english: Having discerned, among friends, both the rising of affection and its waning, and having weighed the two—he who would bear a heavy burden, that one alone the wise man should declare to be a true and steadfast friend.

sanskrit: etān mayoktāṃs tava rājadharmān; nṛṇāṃ ca guptau matim ādadhatsva avāpsyase puṇyaphalaṃ sukhena; sarvo hi lokottamadharmamūlaḥ
english: These duties of a king that I have declared to you, set your mind upon them, and upon the protection of men; thus shall you easily win the fruit of merit, for the whole world is rooted in the highest dharma.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca ayaṃ pitāmahenokto rājadharmaḥ sanātanaḥ īśvaraś ca mahādaṇḍo daṇḍe sarvaṃ pratiṣṭhitam
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: This eternal dharma of kings has been declared by you, grandfather, and the great Rod is sovereign; upon the Rod everything rests.

sanskrit: devatānām ṛṣīṇāṃ ca pitṝṇāṃ ca mahātmanām yakṣarakṣaḥpiśācānāṃ martyānāṃ ca viśeṣataḥ
english: Of the gods, of the seers, and of the great-souled ancestors, of yakṣas, rākṣasas, and piśācas, and of mortals especially—

sanskrit: sarveṣāṃ prāṇināṃ loke tiryakṣv api nivāsinām sarvavyāpī mahātejā daṇḍaḥ śreyān iti prabho
english: of all living beings in the world, and of those that dwell among the beasts as well, the Rod, all-pervading and of mighty splendour, is the supreme good, O lord.

sanskrit: ity etad uktaṃ bhavatā sarvaṃ daṇḍyaṃ carācaram dṛśyate lokam āsaktaṃ sasurāsuramānuṣam
english: Thus has it been declared by you that all things, moving and unmoving, are subject to the Rod; and the world is seen to cling to it—gods, asuras, and men alike.

sanskrit: etad icchāmy ahaṃ jñātuṃ tattvena bharatarṣabha ko daṇḍaḥ kīdṛśo daṇḍaḥ kiṃrūpaḥ kiṃparāyaṇaḥ
english: This I wish to know in its true essence, O bull of the Bhāratas: What is the Rod? Of what kind is the Rod? What is its form? What is its final ground?

sanskrit: kimātmakaḥ kathaṃbhūtaḥ katimūrtiḥ kathaṃprabhuḥ jāgarti sa kathaṃ daṇḍaḥ prajāsv avahitātmakaḥ
english: What is its nature? How does it come to be? How many forms does it bear? How does it hold sway? How does that Rod keep watch, attentive of spirit, over the people?

sanskrit: kaś ca pūrvāparam idaṃ jāgarti paripālayan kaś ca vijñāyate pūrvaṃ ko 'paro daṇḍasaṃjñitaḥ kiṃsaṃsthaś ca bhaved daṇḍaḥ kā cāsya gatir iṣyate
english: And who is it that keeps watch, guarding this realm of before and after? Which is known to be the prior, and which the other that is named the Rod? In what does the Rod abide, and what is held to be its course?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca śṛṇu kauravya yo daṇḍo vyavahāryo yathā ca saḥ yasmin hi sarvam āyattaṃ sa daṇḍa iha kevalaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Hear, O Kaurava, what the Rod is and how it is administered; for that on which all things depend, that alone is the Rod here.

sanskrit: dharmasyākhyā mahārāja vyavahāra itīṣyate tasya lopaḥ kathaṃ na syāl lokeṣv avahitātmanaḥ ity arthaṃ vyavahārasya vyavahāratvam iṣyate
english: The name of dharma, great king, is held to be 'administration of justice' (vyavahāra); for that which is heedful in the worlds, how should its abolition come to pass? It is for this purpose that the administration of justice holds its character as such.

sanskrit: api caitat purā rājan manunā proktam āditaḥ supraṇītena daṇḍena priyāpriyasamātmanā prajā rakṣati yaḥ samyag dharma eva sa kevalaḥ
english: Moreover this was declared of old by Manu at the very beginning, O king: he who rightly protects his subjects with a well-administered Rod, even-minded toward friend and foe alike—he alone is dharma itself.

sanskrit: athoktam etad vacanaṃ prāg eva manunā purā janma coktaṃ vasiṣṭhena brahmaṇo vacanaṃ mahat
english: Now this saying was uttered first of all by Manu in olden times, and its origin too was declared by Vasiṣṭha—the great word of Brahmā.

sanskrit: prāg idaṃ vacanaṃ proktam ataḥ prāgvacanaṃ viduḥ vyavahārasya cākhyānād vyavahāra ihocyate
english: Because this saying was uttered first, men know it as the 'prior word'; and from the telling of the administration of justice, it is here called vyavahāra.

sanskrit: daṇḍāt trivargaḥ satataṃ supraṇītāt pravartate daivaṃ hi paramo daṇḍo rūpato 'gnir ivocchikhaḥ
english: From the Rod, well-administered, the threefold aim of life ever proceeds; for the Rod is the supreme divine power, in form like fire with upward-leaping flame.

sanskrit: nīlotpaladalaśyāmaś caturdaṃṣṭraś caturbhujaḥ aṣṭapān naikanayanaḥ śaṅkukarṇordhvaromavān
english: Dark as the petal of the blue lotus, four-fanged and four-armed, eight-footed, many-eyed, with pointed ears and bristling hair,

sanskrit: jaṭī dvijihvas tāmrāsyo mṛgarājatanucchadaḥ etad rūpaṃ bibharty ugraṃ daṇḍo nityaṃ durāvaraḥ
english: matted-locked, double-tongued, copper-faced, clad in the hide of the lion, king of beasts—this terrible form the Rod ever bears, hard to withstand.

sanskrit: asir gadā dhanuḥ śaktis triśūlaṃ mudgaraḥ śaraḥ musalaṃ paraśuś cakraṃ prāso daṇḍarṣṭitomarāḥ
english: Sword and mace, bow and spear, trident, hammer and arrow, pestle, axe and discus, the javelin, the staff, the lance, and the iron pike—

sanskrit: sarvapraharaṇīyāni santi yānīha kāni cit daṇḍa eva hi sarvātmā loke carati mūrtimān
english: whatever weapons of war there are at all here, the Rod, being the soul of them all, moves embodied through the world.

sanskrit: bhindaṃś chindan rujan kṛntan dārayan pāṭayaṃs tathā ghātayann abhidhāvaṃś ca daṇḍa eva caraty uta
english: Splitting, cleaving, crushing, slicing, rending, and tearing asunder, slaying and charging onward—the Rod alone moves abroad.

sanskrit: asir viśasano dharmas tīkṣṇavartmā durāsadaḥ śrīgarbho vijayaḥ śāstā vyavahāraḥ prajāgaraḥ
english: It is the Sword, the Slayer, Dharma, the Keen-pathed, the Unassailable, Womb-of-fortune, Victory, the Chastiser, Administration-of-justice, the Watcher-over-subjects;

sanskrit: śāstraṃ brāhmaṇamantraś ca śāstā prāgvacanaṃ gataḥ dharmapālo 'kṣaro devaḥ satyago nityago grahaḥ
english: the Scripture, the Brāhmaṇa's spell, the Chastiser who has become the prior word, Guardian-of-dharma, the Imperishable, the God, the Truth-faring, the Ever-faring, the Seizer;

sanskrit: asaṅgo rudratanayo manujyeṣṭhaḥ śivaṃkaraḥ nāmāny etāni daṇḍasya kīrtitāni yudhiṣṭhira
english: the Unattached, son of Rudra, eldest of men, bringer of weal—these names of the Rod have been recounted, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: daṇḍo hi bhagavān viṣṇur yajño nārāyaṇaḥ prabhuḥ śaśvad rūpaṃ mahad bibhran mahāpuruṣa ucyate
english: For the Rod is the Lord Viṣṇu, the Sacrifice, Nārāyaṇa the master; bearing forever its great form, it is called the Supreme Being.

sanskrit: yathoktā brahmakanyeti lakṣmīr nītiḥ sarasvatī daṇḍanītir jagaddhātrī daṇḍo hi bahuvigrahaḥ
english: As she is called the daughter of Brahmā—Lakṣmī, Polity, Sarasvatī—the science of governance by the Rod is the sustainer of the world; for the Rod is of many bodies.

sanskrit: arthānarthau sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ dharmādharmau balābale daurbhāgyaṃ bhāgadheyaṃ ca puṇyāpuṇye guṇāguṇau
english: Gain and loss, pleasure and pain, dharma and its opposite, strength and weakness, ill fortune and good fortune, merit and demerit, virtue and its absence,

sanskrit: kāmākāmāv ṛtur māsaḥ śarvarī divasaḥ kṣaṇaḥ aprasādaḥ prasādaś ca harṣaḥ krodhaḥ śamo damaḥ
english: desire and aversion, season and month, night and day and moment, displeasure and grace, joy, anger, calm and restraint,

sanskrit: daivaṃ puruṣakāraś ca mokṣāmokṣau bhayābhaye hiṃsāhiṃse tapo yajñaḥ saṃyamo 'tha viṣāviṣam
english: fate and human effort, release and bondage, fear and fearlessness, harm and harmlessness, austerity, sacrifice, self-control, and poison and its absence,

sanskrit: antaś cādiś ca madhyaṃ ca kṛtyānāṃ ca prapañcanam madaḥ pramādo darpaś ca dambho dhairyaṃ nayānayau
english: the end, the beginning, and the middle, and the unfolding of all deeds; intoxication, negligence, and arrogance, hypocrisy, steadfastness, right conduct and wrong;

sanskrit: aśaktiḥ śaktir ity eva mānastambhau vyayāvyayau vinayaś ca visargaś ca kālākālau ca bhārata
english: incapacity and capacity, pride and rigidity, expense and saving, discipline and emission, the timely and the untimely, O Bhārata;

sanskrit: anṛtaṃ jñājñatā satyaṃ śraddhāśraddhe tathaiva ca klībatā vyavasāyaś ca lābhālābhau jayājayau
english: falsehood, knowledge and ignorance, truth, and faith and faithlessness likewise, cowardice and resolve, gain and loss, victory and defeat;

sanskrit: tīkṣṇatā mṛdutā mṛtyur āgamānāgamau tathā virāddhiś caiva rāddhiś ca kāryākārye balābale
english: harshness and gentleness, death, arrival and non-arrival, failure and success, what should and should not be done, strength and weakness;

sanskrit: asūyā cānasūyā ca dharmādharmau tathaiva ca apatrapānapatrape hrīś ca saṃpad vipac ca ha
english: envy and freedom from envy, dharma and its opposite likewise, shamelessness and shame, modesty, prosperity and adversity—

sanskrit: tejaḥ karmaṇi pāṇḍityaṃ vākśaktis tattvabuddhitā evaṃ daṇḍasya kauravya loke 'smin bahurūpatā
english: splendour in action, learning, power of speech, insight into truth: such, O Kaurava, is the manifold form of the Rod in this world.

sanskrit: na syād yadīha daṇḍo vai pramatheyuḥ parasparam bhayād daṇḍasya cānyonyaṃ ghnanti naiva yudhiṣṭhira
english: Were there no Rod here, men would crush one another; it is for fear of the Rod that they do not slay one another, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: daṇḍena rakṣyamāṇā hi rājann aharahaḥ prajāḥ rājānaṃ vardhayantīha tasmād daṇḍaḥ parāyaṇam
english: Guarded day by day by the Rod, O king, the subjects make the king prosper here; therefore the Rod is the final refuge.

sanskrit: vyavasthāpayati kṣipram imaṃ lokaṃ nareśvara satye vyavasthito dharmo brāhmaṇeṣv avatiṣṭhate
english: Swiftly it sets this world in order, O lord of men. Dharma, established upon truth, abides among the brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit: dharmayuktā dvijāḥ śreṣṭhā vedayuktā bhavanti ca babhūva yajño vedebhyo yajñaḥ prīṇāti devatāḥ
english: The foremost twice-born, joined to dharma, become joined to the Veda; from the Vedas arose sacrifice, and sacrifice gladdens the gods.

sanskrit: prītāś ca devatā nityam indre paridadaty uta annaṃ dadāti śakraś cāpy anugṛhṇann imāḥ prajāḥ
english: And the gods, ever well pleased, deliver their gifts to Indra; and Śakra in turn gives food, showing favour to these subjects.

sanskrit: prāṇāś ca sarvabhūtānāṃ nityam anne pratiṣṭhitāḥ tasmāt prajāḥ pratiṣṭhante daṇḍo jāgarti tāsu ca
english: And the life-breaths of all beings ever rest upon food; therefore the people stand firm, and the Rod keeps watch over them.

sanskrit: evaṃprayojanaś caiva daṇḍaḥ kṣatriyatāṃ gataḥ rakṣan prajāḥ prajāgarti nityaṃ suvihito 'kṣaraḥ
english: And serving such a purpose, the Rod has passed into kṣatriyahood; protecting the subjects it keeps ever watch, well-ordained and imperishable.

sanskrit: īśvaraḥ puruṣaḥ prāṇaḥ sattvaṃ vittaṃ prajāpatiḥ bhūtātmā jīva ity eva nāmabhiḥ procyate 'ṣṭabhiḥ
english: Lord, Person, Breath, Being, Wealth, Lord-of-creatures, Soul-of-beings, and Living-self—by these eight names it is proclaimed.

sanskrit: adadad daṇḍa evāsmai dhruvam aiśvaryam eva ca bale nayaś ca saṃyuktaḥ sadā pañcavidhātmakaḥ
english: The Rod alone bestowed upon him both abiding sovereignty and lordship; joined with power and statecraft, it is ever fivefold in nature.

sanskrit: kulabāhudhanāmātyāḥ prajñā coktā balāni ca āhāryaṃ cāṣṭakair dravyair balam anyad yudhiṣṭhira
english: Lineage, arms, wealth, ministers, and wisdom are declared to be the forces; and another force, O Yudhiṣṭhira, is to be acquired by the eight kinds of resources.

sanskrit: hastino 'śvā rathāḥ pattir nāvo viṣṭis tathaiva ca daiśikāś cārakāś caiva tad aṣṭāṅgaṃ balaṃ smṛtam
english: Elephants, horses, chariots, foot-soldiers, ships, and corvée labour likewise, guides and spies—that is remembered as the eightfold army.

sanskrit: aṣṭāṅgasya tu yuktasya hastino hastiyāyinaḥ aśvārohāḥ padātāś ca mantriṇo rasadāś ca ye
english: Of this well-equipped eightfold force there are the elephants and their riders, the horsemen and the foot-soldiers, the ministers, and those who supply provisions,

sanskrit: bhikṣukāḥ prāḍvivākāś ca mauhūrtā daivacintakāḥ kośo mitrāṇi dhānyaṃ ca sarvopakaraṇāni ca
english: the mendicant agents and the judges, the astrologers and the readers of omens, the treasury, the allies, the grain, and all the implements.

sanskrit: saptaprakṛti cāṣṭāṅgaṃ śarīram iha yad viduḥ rājyasya daṇḍa evāṅgaṃ daṇḍaḥ prabhava eva ca
english: What they here know to be the seven-membered, eight-limbed body of the kingdom—of that the Rod is the very limb, and the Rod is its very source.

sanskrit: īśvareṇa prayatnena dhāraṇe kṣatriyasya hi daṇḍo dattaḥ samānātmā daṇḍo hīdaṃ sanātanam rājñāṃ pūjyatamo nānyo yathādharmapradarśanaḥ
english: By the Lord, through effort, for the kṣatriya to uphold, the Rod was given, even-souled; for this Rod is eternal. Among kings none other is more worthy of worship than he who reveals dharma as it is.

sanskrit: brahmaṇā lokarakṣārthaṃ svadharmasthāpanāya ca bhartṛpratyaya utpanno vyavahāras tathāparaḥ tasmād yaḥ sahito dṛṣṭo bhartṛpratyayalakṣaṇaḥ
english: By Brahmā, for the protection of the world and for the establishing of each one's own dharma, there arose, resting on the sovereign's authority, yet another administration of justice; hence that which is seen conjoined with it bears the mark of the sovereign's authority.

sanskrit: vyavahāras tu vedātmā vedapratyaya ucyate maulaś ca naraśārdūla śāstroktaś ca tathāparaḥ
english: But administration of justice whose essence is the Veda is called that which rests on the Veda's authority; it is original, O tiger among men, and yet another kind is that taught by the law-books.

sanskrit: ukto yaś cāpi daṇḍo 'sau bhartṛpratyayalakṣaṇaḥ jñeyo na sa narendrastho daṇḍapratyaya eva ca
english: And that Rod which has been spoken of, bearing the mark of the sovereign's authority, is to be known as resting in the lord of men, and as resting on the Rod's own authority.

sanskrit: daṇḍapratyayadṛṣṭo 'pi vyavahārātmakaḥ smṛtaḥ vyavahāraḥ smṛto yaś ca sa vedaviṣayātmakaḥ
english: Though seen as resting on the Rod's authority, it is remembered as being of the nature of administration of justice; and that which is remembered as administration of justice has its essence in the domain of the Veda.

sanskrit: yaś ca vedaprasūtātmā sa dharmo guṇadarśakaḥ dharmapratyaya utpanno yathādharmaḥ kṛtātmabhiḥ
english: And that whose essence is born of the Veda is dharma, the revealer of virtues; arising upon the authority of dharma, it is dharma as it truly is, made manifest by the perfected of soul.

sanskrit: vyavahāraḥ prajāgoptā brahmadiṣṭo yudhiṣṭhira trīn dhārayati lokān vai satyātmā bhūtivardhanaḥ
english: Administration of justice, the protector of the subjects, ordained by Brahmā, O Yudhiṣṭhira, upholds the three worlds; its essence is truth, and it is the increaser of well-being.

sanskrit: yaś ca daṇḍaḥ sa dṛṣṭo no vyavahāraḥ sanātanaḥ vyavahāraś ca yo dṛṣṭaḥ sa dharma iti naḥ śrutaḥ yaś ca vedaḥ sa vai dharmo yaś ca dharmaḥ sa satpathaḥ
english: That which is the Rod has been seen by us as the eternal administration of justice; and that which has been seen as administration of justice, that we have heard to be dharma; and that which is the Veda is verily dharma, and that which is dharma is the path of the good.

sanskrit: brahmā prajāpatiḥ pūrvaṃ babhūvātha pitāmahaḥ lokānāṃ sa hi sarveṣāṃ sasurāsurarakṣasām samanuṣyoragavatāṃ kartā caiva sa bhūtakṛt
english: Brahmā, the Lord of creatures, was the first to be, the grandfather; for he is the maker of all the worlds—with their gods, asuras, and rākṣasas, with men and serpents—and he is the creator of beings.

sanskrit: tato no vyavahāro 'yaṃ bhartṛpratyayalakṣaṇaḥ tasmād idam avocāma vyavahāranidarśanam
english: Hence this administration of justice of ours bears the mark of the sovereign's authority; and therefore we have spoken this exposition of administration of justice.

sanskrit: mātā pitā ca bhrātā ca bhāryā cātha purohitaḥ nādaṇḍyo vidyate rājñāṃ yaḥ svadharme na tiṣṭhati
english: Mother and father, brother, wife, and household priest—for kings there exists none exempt from the Rod who does not abide in his own dharma.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam aṅgeṣu rājā dyutimān vasuhoma iti śrutaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: On this too they recite this ancient story. Among the Aṅgas there was a radiant king known as Vasuhoma.

sanskrit: sa rājā dharmanityaḥ san saha patnyā mahātapāḥ muñjapṛṣṭhaṃ jagāmātha devarṣigaṇapūjitam
english: That king, ever devoted to dharma and of great austerity, went together with his queen to Muñjapṛṣṭha, honoured by the hosts of divine seers.

sanskrit: tatra śṛṅge himavato merau kanakaparvate yatra muñjavaṭe rāmo jaṭāharaṇam ādiśat
english: There, on a peak of Himavat, on Meru the golden mountain, at the Muñja banyan where Rāma ordained the cutting away of his matted locks—

sanskrit: tadāprabhṛti rājendra ṛṣibhiḥ saṃśitavrataiḥ muñjapṛṣṭha iti proktaḥ sa deśo rudrasevitaḥ
english: from that time onward, O lord of kings, by the seers of strict vows that region, frequented by Rudra, was called Muñjapṛṣṭha.

sanskrit: sa tatra bahubhir yuktaḥ sadā śrutimayair guṇaiḥ brāhmaṇānām anumato devarṣisadṛśo 'bhavat
english: There, endowed with many virtues ever born of sacred lore, approved by the brāhmaṇas, he became the equal of a divine seer.

sanskrit: taṃ kadā cid adīnātmā sakhā śakrasya mānitaḥ abhyāgacchan mahīpālo māndhātā śatrukarśanaḥ
english: Once there came to visit him the undaunted lord of earth, the friend of Śakra and the honoured one, Māndhātā, scourge of his foes.

sanskrit: so 'bhisṛtya tu māndhātā vasuhomaṃ narādhipam dṛṣṭvā prakṛṣṭaṃ tapasā vinayenābhyatiṣṭhata
english: Approaching the king Vasuhoma, and seeing him eminent in austerity, Māndhātā stood before him with humility.

sanskrit: vasuhomo 'pi rājño vai gām arghyaṃ ca nyavedayat aṣṭāṅgasya ca rājyasya papraccha kuśalaṃ tadā
english: Vasuhoma in turn offered the king the cow and the welcome-water, and then inquired after the welfare of his eight-membered kingdom.

sanskrit: sadbhir ācaritaṃ pūrvaṃ yathāvad anuyāyinam apṛcchad vasuhomas taṃ rājan kiṃ karavāṇi te
english: Following duly the usage practised of old by the good, Vasuhoma asked him, O king: 'What may I do for you?'

sanskrit: so 'bravīt paramaprīto māndhātā rājasattamam vasuhomaṃ mahāprājñam āsīnaṃ kurunandana
english: Greatly pleased, Māndhātā spoke to that best of kings, the deeply wise Vasuhoma, as he sat, O delight of the Kurus:

sanskrit: bṛhaspater mataṃ rājann adhītaṃ sakalaṃ tvayā tathaivauśanasaṃ śāstraṃ vijñātaṃ te narādhipa
english: 'The doctrine of Bṛhaspati, O king, you have studied entire, and likewise the treatise of Uśanas is fully known to you, O lord of men.

sanskrit: tad ahaṃ śrotum icchāmi daṇḍa utpadyate katham kiṃ vāpi pūrvaṃ jāgarti kiṃ vā paramam ucyate
english: This I wish to hear: how does the Rod come into being? What is it that keeps watch from the first, and what is said to be supreme?

sanskrit: kathaṃ kṣatriyasaṃsthaś ca daṇḍaḥ saṃpraty avasthitaḥ brūhi me sumahāprājña dadāmy ācāryavetanam
english: And how, abiding in the kṣatriya, does the Rod now stand established? Tell me, O greatly wise one; I shall give you the teacher's fee.'

sanskrit: vasuhoma uvāca śṛṇu rājan yathā daṇḍaḥ saṃbhūto lokasaṃgrahaḥ prajāvinayarakṣārthaṃ dharmasyātmā sanātanaḥ
english: Vasuhoma said: Hear, O king, how the Rod came to be—the sustainer of the world, for the disciplining and protection of the subjects, the eternal soul of dharma.

sanskrit: brahmā yiyakṣur bhagavān sarvalokapitāmahaḥ ṛtvijaṃ nātmanā tulyaṃ dadarśeti hi naḥ śrutam
english: The Lord Brahmā, grandfather of all the worlds, wishing to sacrifice, found no officiating priest equal to himself—so we have heard.

sanskrit: sa garbhaṃ śirasā devo varṣapūgān adhārayat pūrṇe varṣasahasre tu sa garbhaḥ kṣuvato 'patat
english: That god bore an embryo within his head for a multitude of years; and when a full thousand years were complete, the embryo fell forth as he sneezed.

sanskrit: sa kṣupo nāma saṃbhūtaḥ prajāpatir ariṃdama ṛtvig āsīt tadā rājan yajñe tasya mahātmanaḥ
english: He came to be a Lord of creatures named Kṣupa, O subduer of foes; and he then served as the officiating priest at the sacrifice of that great-souled one, O king.

sanskrit: tasmin pravṛtte satre tu brahmaṇaḥ pārthivarṣabha hṛṣṭarūpapracāratvād daṇḍaḥ so 'ntarhito 'bhavat
english: But while that sacrificial session of Brahmā was in progress, O bull among kings, because of the glad and untroubled course of things, that Rod became hidden from view.

sanskrit: tasminn antarhite cātha prajānāṃ saṃkaro 'bhavat naiva kāryaṃ na cākāryaṃ bhojyābhojyaṃ na vidyate
english: And when it had vanished, confusion arose among the subjects: there was no longer what ought to be done nor what ought not, nor what was fit or unfit to eat.

sanskrit: peyāpeyaṃ kutaḥ siddhir hiṃsanti ca parasparam gamyāgamyaṃ tadā nāsīt parasvaṃ svaṃ ca vai samam
english: What was fit or unfit to drink—whence then any right ordering? They fell to harming one another; there was no distinction then of the lawful and the forbidden, and another's property and one's own were held to be the same.

sanskrit: parasparaṃ vilumpante sārameyā ivāmiṣam abalaṃ balino jaghnur nirmaryādam avartata
english: They plundered one another like dogs snatching at meat; the strong slew the weak, and all proceeded without bound or restraint.
